#2263. Joao Pedro double and Caicedo stunner give Chelsea win over AC Milan

Chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

MOISÉS CAICEDO THAT IS INCREDIBLE 🤯 pic.twitter.com/C6CEcUG1sE

Chelsea had further chances to extend their lead in a dominant second-half performance but were unable to add to their three goals.

Chelsea conclude their tour of the Far East with a game against Johor Darul Ta’zim on Sunday in Malaysia before returning home.

Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge before beginning their Premier League campaign at Fulham.

AC Milan take on Amorim’s former club Manchester United next Saturday before they kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

Chelsea managed to lure Austin MacPhee to take care of their set-pieces and today Chelsea scored two goals from corners. Here is a snippet of Mike McGrath’s piece on MacPhee’s arrival at Chelsea:

He is among the new breed of coaches who are rock stars in their own right, taking centre-stage since rules were changed so that only one person is allowed in the technical area at a time. For MacPhee to get closer to the players for a set-piece, it will mean Xabi Alonso taking a step back onto the bench.

It has been an incredible rise for MacPhee, 46, who was working on Michael O’Neill’s staff with Northern Ireland 10 years ago this summer, helping them reach the knockout stages of the European Championship.

Chelsea take on Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia tomorrow before returning to the UK. Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad before taking on Fulham on the opening weekend of the new season.

AC Milan will play Manchester United next weekend and then kick off their Serie A campaign against Torino.

Possession: Chelsea 50%-50% AC MilanShots: 18-5Shots on target: 8-0Corners: 7-2

The final whistle is blown in Jakarta and Chelsea have cruised to a 3-0 win over AC Milan. Goals from Caicedo and a double from Pedro either side of half-time have led Xabi Alonso’s side to the victory. They have one more game out in the Far East before returning home to the UK.

What a performance! 👏 pic.twitter.com/GcUZXwXbRj

Ramos is picked out after making a run into the Chelsea box and is denied by Sanchez. However, the offside flag has gone up anyway against Ramos. AC Milan have barely threatened the Chelsea goal in this second half.

A late change for Chelsea as Sarr replaces Fofana.

Chelsea are seeking their fourth goal as Quenda strikes a shot powerfully from just outside the box but it goes narrowly wide. Xabi Alonso’s side have dominated this second half.

Estevao has the chance to score moments after coming on after good work from the Brazilian down Chelsea’s right but is denied by a good save from Torriani.

Chelsea make a triple changes as Estevao, Mudryk and Watson come on. Mudryk made his return after his doping ban against Juventus during the week.

Chelsea hit the frame of the goal once more. Jackson gets the better of Vladimirov down Chelsea’s left and moves into the AC Milan penalty area. Jackson opens up his body as if he is going to curl his shot into the far corner but instead shoots towards the near corner, with his effort coming off the post.

Ricci goes for an audacious strike with the outside of his right foot from outside the box but his effort misses the target.

Palmer was deep in conversation with his boss Alonso during that water break.

Chelsea made a substitution during that break as Anselmino comes on for Hato. Thus far, Chelsea have made three changes in this game and Alonso did confirm before the game that some players should be able to go the full 90 this far into pre-season.

Chelsea hit the post. Quenda receives the ball on the right side of the penalty area and quickly moves the ball onto his right foot. The 19-year-old then smashes a shot towards goal and the ball flies into the outside of the post. Quenda struck that with some venom.

Palmer has a chance to get Chelsea’s fourth from the left side of the box but AC Milan keeper Torriani makes the save down to his left.

AC Milan have offered very little going forward since the break and Sanchez has not been troubled in the Chelsea goal.

AC Milan have a good chance to get a goal back. Musah finds space on the right side of the box and cuts it back towards the penalty spot. He picks out Nkunku but the former Chelsea man wastes the opportunity.

Palestra is found with a cross from the right to the far post. Palestra takes a touch but his shot goes into the side netting.

Ruben Amorim is demanding a free-kick just outside the Chelsea box but the referee does not agree. Replays show that AC Milan probably should have been given the free-kick as it was a foul by Fofana on Ramos. Both players went down but are back to their feet.

Xabi Alonso is going to make his first two changes of the game as Jackson and Quenda replace Welbeck and Neto.

Chelsea have their third and their new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee will be delighted with that one. Lavia plays a flat delivery from a corner out on the left to Caicedo on the edge of the box. Caicedo hits it first time on the volley with the outside of his right foot and picks out the bottom right corner with perfection.

Chelsea go 2-0 up not even a minute into the second half. Neto, on the right side of the box, cuts onto his preferred left foot and crosses to the far post. Pedro gets on the end of it and, despite the Milan keeper getting a touch on the shot, the ball ends up in the far corner.

AC Milan have made a raft of changes at the break, which includes their new record signing Ramos, who has joined from PSG this summer. Former Chelsea man Nkunku is also on. Milan were back out from the dressing rooms a fair bit earlier than Chelsea were. It is rather farcical how long Chelsea took to re-emerge for the second half and they just saunter out as if nothing is up. Why on earth did the officials just allow Chelsea to take over 20 minutes for half-time?

Nearly 25 minutes after the first half concluded, we are finally back under way in Jakarta.

Possession: Chelsea 58%-42% AC MilanShots: 6-4Shots on target: 3-0Corners: 4-2

The first half in Jakarta is brought an end and Chelsea take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Pedro’s goal on the stroke of half-time.

90 seconds into added time at the end of this first half, we have the first goal in Jakarta. Caicedo’s delivery from the right picks out Pedro, who has a free header inside the six-yard box and makes no mistake, picking out the corner. Pedro really should not have been afforded so much space in the six-yard box.

Palestra makes a run in behind the AC Milan defence and is found but De Winter gets back to put it behind for a corner...

Due to the water break, there will be three additional minutes at the end of this first half.

The first booking of the game goes the way of AC Milan as Pavlovic clears out Palestra. A deserved booking.

Neto and Pedro exchange a good one-two down Chelsea’s right to put the former racing down the right wing. Neto then tries to find Welbeck in the centre of the box but it is just behind him.

Then, moments later, Pedro spurns a great chance for Chelsea. Palestra’s cross from the left is just out of Palmer’s reach but falls straight to Pedro, who blazes over from 12 yards out. He was leaning back and should really be hitting the target.

The space opens up for Palmer to take on a shot from range but his effort is blocked by De Winter. Palmer has not managed to have that much of an effect on this game thus far.

Pavlovic drives forward from his defensive position through the Chelsea half. He gets all the way to the Chelsea box before shooting but he looked to lack conviction, firing off target.

We will pause for a drinks break, which unfortunately we became accustomed to during the World Cup. Palmer takes the chance to take a seat on the bench whilst taking on some fluids.

Neto takes a first-time shot from outside the box and looks to curl it into the far corner, forcing Torriani into a decent save diving down to his right.

That is good one-vs-one defending from Achemapong. Estupinan plays the ball into the path of Leao, who drives through the Chelsea half down AC Milan’s left. As Leao approaches the Chelsea box, Leao attempts to push it past Acheampong but the young Chelsea defender times his sliding challenge to perfection and puts it behind for a corner. Sanchez punches it out to the edge of the box, where Comotto takes it on his chest before volleying towards goal. The ball goes behind for another corner, which Chelsea just about scramble away.

Chelsea hit the post. Palestra drives forward for Chelsea down their left before the ball falls to Welbeck on the left side of the box. Welbeck’s effort hits the outside of the post. AC Milan keeper Torriani appeared though to always have it covered.

Chelsea gift the ball away inside their own half and Leao drives forward. The Portuguese forward moves into the Chelsea penalty area before getting his shot away but his effort is blocked.

A big, big chance for Chelsea to take the lead. A long ball is played forward in behind the AC Milan defence and Pedro gets the better of De Winter inside the Milan penalty area. It is then a one-on-one chance with Torriani but Pedro hits it straight at the Milan goalkeeper. Torriani should have come to claim that long ball and then Pedro should probably have buried that opportunity.

Chelsea win their third corner of the game as Palmer’s cross from the right takes a couple of deflections off AC Milan defender. Captain Caicedo has trotted over to take it out on the left. He sends it into a good area but a foul on the AC Milan keeper Torriani is given against Pedro.

Neto clips a free-kick into the AC Milan penalty area, which is chested down by Pedro. The Brazilian holds the ball up well inside the box before winning a corner. Chelsea play it short and Palmer crosses to the back post, where Palestra wins Chelsea another corner, this time out on the left.

Caicedo’s inswinging delivery is headed away at the front post.

Palestra, who has joined Chelsea this summer from Atalanta, is proving his versatility today; he has mostly operated for Chelsea at right-back so far this pre-season but he is starting at left-back in this game.

Camarda is played in behind the Chelsea defence and tries to get the better of Fofana inside the Chelsea penalty area but the ball just runs out of play across the byline before Camarda can square the ball.

We are under way in Jakarta, Indonesia, in Chelsea’s penultimate game over in the Far East. Before the game started, a huge AC Milan tifo was unveiled at one end of the ground.

It is 7pm in Jakarta yet the temperature is still up at 29 degrees with the humidity at nearly 70%. These conditions will be a proper test for both sides.

The teams emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off in Indonesia.

The trophies won by Franco Baresi, who has died at the age of 66, are their own monument to the AC Milan and Italy defender’s greatness. Six times a Serie A champion, five as captain, three European Cup-winning campaigns, 10 other winners’ medals and the distinction of being a member of Italy squads that finished in first, second and third places at World Cup tournaments demonstrate that his career, in a significantly more meritocratic era, stand alongside the giants even if the bias towards attacking virtuosos denied him the Ballon d’Or his talent deserved.

Yet they do not tell us why the grief, so tangible in Milan and beyond today, transcends tribal rivalry. It would be unfair to say that he transformed the art of Italian defending. Gaetano Scirea, the elegant Juventus sweeper who kept the 21-year-old Baresi confined to the bench when Italy won their third World Cup in 1982, had a surplus of natural ability, composure and intelligence. He did not need the raw-elbowed brutality of Claudio Gentile, heir to generations of Italian defenders influenced by the post-war influx of players brought up in the traditions of Argentina and Uruguay.

INS:Marco Palestra ⇠ Atalanta, £42mGeovany Quenda ⇠ Sporting, £42mMorgan Rogers ⇠ Aston Villa, £117mMaxence Lacroix ⇠ Crystal Palace, £51mDanny Welbeck ⇠ Brighton, UndisclosedJordan Henderson ⇠ Brentford, FreeValentin Barco ⇠ Strasbourg, Undisclosed

OUTS:Andrey Santos ⇢ Manchester United, £50mMarc Cucurella ⇢ Real Madrid, £50mTyrique George ⇢ Everton, £24mAlejandro Garnacho ⇢ Aston Villa, Loan

Chelsea are on the verge of making yet another signing with Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarria close to securing a move to Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea: Sanchez; Palestra, Acheampong, Fofana, Hato; Palmer, Caicedo, Lavia, Neto; Welbeck, Joao Pedro.Substitutes: Sharman-Lowe, Penders, Sarr, Anselmino, Tosin, Subuloye, Essugo, Nicoll-Jazuli, Watson, Walsh, Satpayev, Quenda, Gittens, Estevao, Mudryk, Jackson, Delap.

AC Milan: Torriani; Terracciano, De Winter, Pavlovic; Chukwueze, Modric, Comotto, Estupinan; Loftus-Cheek, Leao; Camarda.Substitutes: Ricci, G. Ramos, Diawara, Nkunku, Fofana, Tomori, Athekame, Odogu, Jashari, Bartesaghi, Vladimirov, Pittarella, Gabbia, Saelemakers, Cisse, Musah.

The English forward joined Chelsea from Borussia Dortmund last summer for just under £50m. He struggled to make an impact last season in his first year at Chelsea, failing to register a goal in the Premier League or Champions League but did spend most of the second half of last season on the sidelines due to an injury. Gittens, who is on the bench for Chelsea today, has been speaking this week to CFC+:

“I am feeling, I would say, more confident now, in my body as well. The injury that happened [impacted my first season], but I am feeling better every day. I am trying to improve every day to be the best version of myself. It has been good to be back with the boys. I am really enjoying it right now and it has been really good to be part of this team.”

Have a great day, Jamie. 🥳 pic.twitter.com/QeX83XrXAM

In Chelsea’s defeat to Juventus in midweek, Ukrainian forward Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 after a long doping ban was resolved. You can read all about that game right here. Mudryk is on the bench for Chelsea today.

Our line-up to face AC Milan! pic.twitter.com/MK2hd0c708

July 28- Western Sydney Wanderers 4 Chelsea 6August 1- Chelsea 1 Tottenham 2August 5- Chelsea 0 Juventus 1Today- Chelsea vs AC MilanAugust 9- Johor Darul Ta’z vs ChelseaAugust 15- Chelsea vs Real Sociedad

Current Chelsea defender Tosin Adarabioyo has been catching up with former Chelsea men Ruben Loftus-Cheek, who starts for AC Milan today, and Fikayo Tomori.

The team news is in from Jakarta! 🗞️ pic.twitter.com/BRBjmlgwz8

The atmosphere is building. 🇮🇩📈 pic.twitter.com/fhXfDVAf6s

Chelsea’s pre-season continues out in the Far East as they take on AC Milan in the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta, Indonesia. Both clubs now have new managers, with Xabi Alonso taking over at Chelsea and former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim now at the helm at AC Milan. These sides met in pre-season last year, with Chelsea winning 4-1 at Stamford Bridge. At that time, now-Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca was in charge whilst Max Allegri, who is now at Napoli, was leading AC Milan. The last time they met competitively was during the 2022/23 Champions League season, with Chelsea winning both games.

Chelsea lost 1-0 to AC Milan’s Serie A rivals Juventus on Wednesday in Hong Kong, in which Danny Welbeck made his first Chelsea appearance after joining from Brighton in the last week.

“We want to have a great team spirit and that is built on a daily basis with a great culture in the building,” Alonso said in his pre-match press conference. “That helps in the moment you have to compete. You feel better having that togetherness, trust, and the bonds between the players are so important to ultimately building a winning mentality, and a team that can compete anywhere. So the football side is so important, but the mental side is as important. And the strength of the team is the most important. We have been able to train and prepare [during pre-season] and I am very happy with the attitude and personality, we know that it is a very important part of this tour.”

It has been another busy week on the transfer front for Chelsea; not only has Welbeck arrived over the last week but so too have Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco. Alonso’s men have two more games after this against Johor Darul Ta’zim and Real Sociedad before getting their Premier League campaign under way with a derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage.

AC Milan finished fifth in Serie A last season to earn a spot in the Europa League last season. Their big-money acquisition this summer as been Portuguese striker Goncalo Ramos from PSG. They have played two pre-season friendlies so far, which have both ended in draws; 2-2 against Celtic and then 1-1 against city rivals Inter. They kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

#2259. Russell Martin ‘spoken highly of’ at Manchester United before Rangers stint

Former Rangers boss Russell Martin was “spoken highly of” by Manchester United technical director Jason Wilcox as the Old Trafford club weighed up potential replacements for Erik ten Hag in 2024.

Wilcox had previously worked with Martin at Southampton and regarded the former Scotland international as a manager worth monitoring for the future.

According to The Athletic, Martin was not considered a realistic candidate for the United job at that stage due to his relative lack of top-level experience, but Wilcox was impressed by his character, tactical understanding and commitment to possession-based football.

Pedro Caixinha back in Europe after joining 13th club of managerial career

Unseen moment Rangers star warned 'job's not done' by team-mate after semi-final win

Ex-Rangers star calls time on playing career after 17 years

Martin would later take charge of Rangers, but his spell at Ibrox proved ill-fated, lasting just 123 days. It proved another setback in Martin’s managerial career after his time with Southampton had ended in relegation from the Premier League.

But the revelation of Wilcox’s admiration provides an intriguing insight into how highly Martin was regarded before his eventual move to Rangers.

Wilcox had appointed him at Southampton in 2023 and backed him through a difficult start before the club embarked on a club-record 25-match unbeaten run and secured promotion to the Premier League through the play-offs.

#2258. Pancaro: “L'unica cosa che non deve fare la Lazio è quella di mettersi pressione”

Dall'avvio da record alla gestione della pressione: l'analisi di Giuseppe Pancaro sulla straordinaria partenza biancoceleste.

Giuseppe Pancaro, intervenuto ai microfoni di Radiosei, ha analizzato il super momento della Lazio: la forza del gruppo, i successi senza pubblico e la gestione saggia degli obiettivi futuri.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Come sto vivendo questo momento Lazio? E' una Lazio bellissima, non è un momento. Ventotto punti in 10 gare non è un caso. C'è del valore, grande merito da parte di Gattuso. Finalmente anche la soddisfazione per i tifosi che da anni non sognavano più e adesso stanno gioendo.

Ancora più sorprendente fare questi risultati senza tifosi all'Olimpico? Questo è un ulteriore merito di questo gruppo perché la difficoltà ambientale è oggettiva da anni. La sensazione è che loro ora non avvertano questo problema. Sicuramente giocare una gara come quella col Cagliari davanti a 13000 spettatori rispetto ad uno stadio pieno qualcosa toglie sempre. Questa squadra è talmente forte, concentrata, unita e compatta che riesce ad andare oltre.

C'è un momento in ogni stagione in cui ci si accorge che l'obiettivo postosi è cambiato. Quale sarà questo momento in cui magari dai 40 punti si passa a pensare ad una coppa europea? Gattuso in tal senso è bravissimo. L'unica cosa che non deve fare la Lazio è quella di mettersi pressione. Eventualmente penso se ne possa parlare in primavera, al momento fanno benissimo a giocare pensando ad una gara alla volta senza mettersi addosso pressione.

#2257. Fabregas: "Bella serata ma piedi per terra! Domenica partita importante con l'Inter, dobbiamo..."

Fabregas: "Bella serata ma piedi per terra! Domenica partita importante con l'Inter, dobbiamo..."

Cesc Fabregas, tecnico del Como, intervenuto ai microfoni di Sky Sport dopo lo strabiliante vittoria per 9-1 contro il Lens, ha parlato così: "E' una serata felice, questo è il calcio: oggi è andato tutto dalla nostra parte. Bravi ragazzi, ora pensiamo ad una partita molto importante domenica: dobbiamo finire come possiamo al meglio. E' una bella serata per il Como e per i ragazzi: però piedi a terra, umiltà e continuare a lavorare. Dobbiamo imparare ma non per fare il fenomeno, ma per dire che continuiamo così a fare belle prestazioni.

Gol subito? Sì sono arrabbiato, abbiamo cambiato qualcosina: l'ha fatto un mio ex compagno e non l'ho mai visto fare un gol così. Quando ho visto che le ultime due erano PSG e Barcellona ho pensato che dovevamo fare più punti all'inizio: sono due squadre superiori. Mancano tante partite a gennaio: penso a recuperare tanti giocatori che mancano. E' questa la cosa più importante, in attacco mancano in tanti. Dobbiamo fare l'ultimo sprint domenica provando a fare una bella partita e poi riposarsi, ne abbiamo bisogno".

#2256. Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount

Michael Carrick said he had to be careful with Mason Mount after the England midfielder handed Manchester United an injury scare in their friendly draw with Paris St Germain.

Mount has had a torrid time with injuries since signing from Chelsea in a £55m-deal three years ago, starting only 25 Premier League games for United in that time.

The 27-year-old has been successfully deployed by Carrick in a central midfield role during pre-season, leading to speculation that United may not make another expected signing in that department.

But Mount played only 18 minutes of Saturday’s 1-1 draw against the European champions in Gothenburg before being replaced by Scotland international Tyler Fletcher.

“He [Mount] got kicked. We just wanted to be careful and look after him,” Carrick, the United head coach, told reporters in Sweden.

“We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.”

Post-match video footage showed Mount walking freely on to the United bus without the aid of a protective boot or knee support.

Michael Carrick told VG Mason Mount was taken off as a precaution. Looked OK leaving stadium. pic.twitter.com/Uo0fBtgpAl

United went behind within two minutes at the Ullevi Stadium when Liverpool target Ibrahim Mbaye punished slack marking to put PSG ahead.

Bryan Mbeumo fired United level after 32 minutes following good work from Amad Diallo, the Cameroon forward’s third goal in two games after his match-winning double against Atletico Madrid.

United meet Leeds in a Dublin friendly on Wednesday before coming up against AC Milan and their former manager Ruben Amorim next Saturday.

United open their Premier League campaign at Hull on August 22.

“It was good game. PSG is good so we had to keep building fitness. I am happy to have other [players] back and we have to keep going.”

“It’s good for me. I enjoyed it. We need to build fitness, we have a big season ahead.”

“It’s a good game PSG are tough to beat and we got a draw and now think about the next game [against Leeds in Dublin].”

“We have two more games against Leeds a and Milan. We need to have big season and hope to win a trophy.”

All over in Gothenburg and it’s been a good match for Michael Carrick’s team. They looked sharper and quicker than their win over Atletico Madrid last week (what the manager wanted) and things are moving in the right direction. Two things to worry about, however, were the early exits of Mason Mount and Tom Heaton with injuries. They’ll especially hope the Mount knock isn’t anything mid or long term.

Nearly done and it’s been a good run out for United. They’ve looked the better, sharper side and, if anything, deserve to win. In mitigation, this is United fourth pre-season game to PSG’s second...

Fernandes has one thing on his mind when he gets the ball 25 yards out in the centre of the park - a shot. He unleashes the attempt, destined for the bottom-left corner, forcing Longoni, the sub goalkeeper, into a good save.

Two chances for United in quick succession. A lovely ball from the middle of the park by Zirkzee finds Dalot on the right. He chips the ball to the back post where one of the Fletchers (sorry, I am not sure which) heads for goal. His attempt is blocked and the ball, ultimately, falls at the feet of Lacey whose shot is blazed high over the bar.

There have been plenty of good things for Carrick to take from this match. The passing, while not of the standard of a cut-and-thrust Premier League match, has been good for the time of year, and there have been enough flashes of brilliance/class/invention etc to suggest that pre-season is moving in the right direction.

Lovely bit of play by United. A great pass with the outside of the boot from the inside-left channel by Tielemans finds Fernandes who plays a sidefooted shot that goes just wide.

Tielemans’s first bit of brilliance from the Belgian there.

Both sides losing possession a fair bit at the moment. Strong pre-season vibes right now.

Maguire has had a good game. He’s played a number of long passes from the back and looked assured. This time he’s up in the PSG half and decides to have a pop - his shot testing Safanov, who saves well.

Had there been VAR Safanov might have had something to answer for...he may have beaten Zirkzee to the ball but he flew in the air and jurt the United man in the process.

Anwway, there’s no VAR (hurrah, for those of you who consider it a modern-day evil) and it doesn’t matter.

Chance for United to go ahead and it comes from two things. (i) A long, hopeful ball from Fernandes that looks for Zirkzee (ii) Safanov rushing off his line and into no-man’s land. The ball comes loose and Jack Fletcher, instead of having a go at goal, with the keeper on the ground and out of the game, passes to Lacey whose shot is wide.

Tyler Fletcher loses the ball near the United half and it, ultimately, results in a PSG corner. From the set piece United defend well and snuff out all hint of danger.

PSG seeing more of the ball at the moment. They work the ball to the right and Amass brings down Mbaye.

From the resulting free-kick, in the final third, the French side whip in the ball but Mee is up ot the challenge and come to collect well.

Santos, Mbeumo, Shaw, Amad, Lacey are off

Fernandes, Jack Feltcher, Zirkzee and Amass are on.

A raft of changes for PSG sees Marquinhos and João Neves, among others, come on. More like it, in terms of first-team ‘names’, on the pitch for the European Cup champions.

United on top in this half, as they were in the first.

The paces quickens and the game is much better for it. Mbuemo drives toward the PSG box, he cuts inside from the right before unleashing a shot that is bound for the back of the net before a fine one-handed save by Safanov. Credit, too, for Maguire whose long ball from the back found Mbuemo brilliantly. Promising...

Lacey tries to play in Dorgu on the left but he’s asking too much of his team-mate. Wonder when the expected raft of changes will take place?

Slow start to the second half. This is very much pre-season-friendly pace.

Having seen Mount limp off in the first half, there’s more worry at the start of the second and Heaton is force off with what looks like a hamstrung injury. He dashed off his line to clear a ball and in doing so has tweaked something. Mee replaces him.

Back under way Gothenburg - there have been a number of changes and will bring them to you once I’ve worked out who has come on and who they’ve replaced.

A world record that still stands...(this was back in 1995).

And that is it for the first 45 minutes. PSG took the early lead, but from that moment on United have been the better side and deservedly are level through Mbueno’s goal.

There will be one minute of added time at the end of what has been a good first half for Man Utd.

Amad has a go from outside the box forcing the save from Safanov. He’s such a live wire and one of the best in his position in the top flight. Him or Antony? No contest, strange it took United a while to work that one out.

Yet more good work from the underrated Amad. He again closes down well on the right before winning back possession and cutting the ball back for Lacey. To think he was starring for Sunderland in the Championship while Antony was starting for United...

United have been the better side since conceding earlier and, as if to illustrate my point, as I typed that an Mbuemo free-kick is well saved by Safanov. That was heading for the top-right bin.

Great work on the left by Dorgu and Shaw ends with the latter chipping the ball to the back post where Amad is lurking with intent. The Ivorian looks to head the ball home, but before he can get anything on it it looks as though he’s pushed in the back. United players are sure it’s a penalty but, more importantly, the referee doesn’t.

Amad does brilliantly, winning the ball off Koukaba in the final third, from there he scampers toward the box before playing in Mbuemo who takes one touch before firing in a shot into the bottom right corner of the net.

Free-kick for PSG on the right, near the final third. The ball comes in and it’s straight into the arms of Heaton in the United goal.

Kvaratskhelia, not seen much of him so far, runs into the box, but Amad does well to usher him back out.

The match is pedestrian at the moment, but as I type that, Dorgu, yep, him again, drives down the left and puts in a good cross that is well intercepted by Safanov in the PSG goal.

United continue to see more of the ball, Dorgu’s seeing more of it than most. But, no chances really fashioned, still, plenty of time to go.

Worry for United having to sub off Mount. It looks as though he took a knock to a foot and Carrick and co will hope it’s not a long-term injury. Mount, who’s had a good pre-season, has been replaced by Fletcher, son of Darren.

Foul on Mazraoui results in two things. The Mount has to come off, and, United have a free-kick on the edge of the PSG area.

From the set-piece Mbuemo has a go and it’s a regulation save from Safonov in the PSG goal.

Heaven loses possession in the middle of the park and from there it’s like the parting of the Red Sea as PSG have a three-on-one. Mbaye gets the shot in on goal but Andrey Santos covers back brilliantly and does enough to get something on the ball. He’s started both this match and pre-season well.

United are looking half decent on the ball. They’re passing it well and not afraid to switch things around.

A lovely long ball from Maguire finds Dorgo whose lovely first touch takes him into the box before a cut back is intercepted by a PSG man. Promising signs though for Carrick’s men.

United seeing more of the ball at the moment. They’re being patient but cannot fashion an opening and the ball is worked all the way back to Heaton in goal.

Needless to say this is being played at a slowish pace...no blood-and-guts challenges being put in.

Good work down the right sees Amad plays in Shay Lacey who crosses into the box. The ball find shte head of Mbuemo and the ball sails over the bar. Better from United.

United started slowly against Atletico and they’ve done the same here.

Bright start to say the least from the French side. They work the ball left and it’s an easy cross from Dro Fernandez for Mbaye to tap home for the very early lead.

They’re under way in Sweden. United are in their new vibrant red kit and PSG in their blue, red and white kit. Big fan of the French side’s kit, it harks back to the kit they had in the 1990s when the likes of George Weah and David Ginola were entertaining in the capital of France.

Man Utd: Heaton, Mazraoui, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw, Mount, Santos, Dorgu, Lacey, Amad, Mbeumo; Subs: Heath, Mee, Amass, Armer, Dalot, Yoro, Fernandes, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Tielemans, Zirkzee

Paris St-Germain: Safonov, Pacho, Zabarnyi, Koukaba, Boly, Beraldo, Dro, Mayulu, Kvaratskhelia, Ayari, Mbaye; Subs: Marquinhos, Mendes, Lucea, Vitinha, Neves, El Nay, Idder, Drame, Bourdin, Ndjantou, Meite, Longoni, Chevalier

And here’s a famous match that took place there, giving a certain Sir Alex Ferguson his first European trophy.

“Get a bit sharper, get better on the ball, go up a notch.”

“It’s not about today it’s about preparing. Some players have played 90 minutes, some have played three games, some have just come back. So it’s about keeping working on things we’ve been working on.”

“They’re similar to us, but have fewer senior players available . They’ve had a great time and great squad so whoever on the pitch it will be a test.”

A hugely talented player for a number of clubs, including United, who ever really lived up to his early promise.

Good to have you back, lads 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/3EgkXLqcQm

📃 Le onze de départ pour cette rencontre de préparation face à Manchester United. #PSGMUN pic.twitter.com/LodcDM1Yrm

I expect they’ll make an appearence at some point.

Ready to face PSG in our latest pre-season test ✊

Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Kick-off is set for 4pm so stay here for the build up, team news and action.

#2253. Lazio, Liverani frena sullo scudetto: Gattuso pensa gara per gara

L’ex centrocampista guarda alla trasferta di Napoli: una buona prestazione darebbe entusiasmo durante la sosta.

La Lazio è prima da sola, ma Fabio Liverani invita a non parlare ancora di scudetto. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, L’ex centrocampista biancoceleste considera la qualificazione in Champions League un grande risultato e condivide la scelta di Rino Gattuso di affrontare una partita alla volta. In collegamento con Radio Sei, durante la trasmissione Quelli che hanno portato il calcio a Roma, ha parlato anche della prossima sfida con il Napoli, della vittoria sul Cagliari e di Belahyane e Isaksen.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

La trasferta di Napoli è, per Liverani, un’occasione per arrivare alla sosta con ulteriore entusiasmo. Conta il risultato, ma conta anche la prova della squadra: «Fare bene a Napoli sarebbe la ciliegina sulla torta. Un risultato positivo, ma soprattutto una prestazione positiva, permetterebbe di lavorare durante la sosta con grande entusiasmo». L’ex biancoceleste ricorda che la Lazio raggiungerà comunque la pausa da capolista, indipendentemente dall’esito della gara.

Sulle ambizioni stagionali, invece, il suo auspicio è preciso: «Auguro alla Lazio di arrivare in Champions League. Parlare di scudetto è difficile, ma anche la Champions, considerando quello che si diceva in estate, sarebbe un grande risultato». Liverani richiama la lunghezza del campionato e le insidie ancora da affrontare. Per questo approva l’approccio di Gattuso, concentrato su una gara alla volta: a suo giudizio, il tecnico ha costruito così il percorso della squadra.

Liverani torna poi sul successo contro il Cagliari, arrivato nella terza partita in sette giorni. La Lazio, osserva, non è stata brillante. Proprio per questo dà valore al risultato: «Vincere una gara del genere ha un significato importante, perché dimostra che questa squadra ha raggiunto una certa maturità».

Secondo l’ex centrocampista, la posizione in classifica porta anche una maggiore attenzione da parte delle avversarie, che proveranno a contenere i principali pericoli biancocelesti. Cita il Cagliari e la scelta di schierare Fadera. La vittoria, nella sua lettura, è stata diversa dalle altre: la Lazio è riuscita a portarla a casa pur incontrando difficoltà.

#2252. Martin O'Neill and Celtic chiefs given ‘hard but fair’ grilling at recent meeting

Celtic manager Martin O’Neill and senior club figures faced more than two hours of “hard but fair” questioning from supporters at a packed meeting in Greenock.

Around 120 fans attended the Greenock Celtic Supporters’ Club on Monday night, with recruitment, transfer policy, communication and the club’s ambitions and strategy among the issues raised.

Per Celtic's statement on what transpired, O’Neill was joined by interim chairman Brian Wilson, chief executive Michael Nicholson, chief financial officer Chris McKay and other club officials for the two-and-a-half-hour question-and-answer session.

Wilson admitted the Celtic hierarchy had been prepared for tough questioning.

He said: “We didn’t expect an easy ride and didn’t get one, but the meeting was conducted in a constructive and mutually respectful way and the messages delivered by supporters will be taken on board and learned from.”

Celtic Fans Collective demand Dermot Desmond attend AGM in person and face scrutiny

Celtic Europa League rivals make shock decision to sack history-making boss

Furious Besiktas star turns on team-mates ahead of crunch Celtic showdown

Supporters from Greenock, Port Glasgow, Gourock, Johnny Doyle, Port Glasgow Hibs and Largs clubs were among those represented.

Nicholson also welcomed the opportunity to hear directly from fans and insisted everyone involved shared the same desire to see Celtic succeed.

He said: “Everyone in the room wants the best for Celtic and that was evident.

“We are grateful for supporters’ input and look forward to continuing to meet with supporters as we work on improving communication and engagement in the weeks and months ahead.”

Celtic say further details on the club’s new Celtic Connect engagement initiative and future fans’ forums will be announced soon.

The Greenock gathering followed recent meetings with the Affiliation of Registered CSCs in Glasgow and the Association of Irish Celtic Supporters' Clubs in Cork.

#2249. ESCLUSIVA - Inter, sorpassate Fiorentina e Ajax per Stefan Ćapin. Può arrivare già a gennaio

ESCLUSIVA - Inter, sorpassate Fiorentina e Ajax per Stefan Ćapin. Può arrivare già a gennaio

Installa la nostra App gratuita e accedi più velocemente alle notizie

Mentre navighi nell'app, scorri il dito da sinistra a destra dello schermo per tornare alle pagine precedenti

L'Inter continua a lavorare con grande attenzione sul mercato dei giovani e potrebbe presto assicurarsi un altro talento di prospettiva. Secondo quanto raccolto da FCINTER1908.IT, i nerazzurri sono molto avanti nella corsa a Stefan Ćapin, centrocampista offensivo classe 2011 considerato uno dei profili più interessanti della sua generazione.

Scegli Fcinter1908.it come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui

La concorrenza non mancava, ma l'Inter sembra aver guadagnato un vantaggio importante sulle altre società interessate.

Nato a Belgrado il 13 gennaio 2011, Ćapin ha nazionalità slovena ed è già nel giro delle rappresentative giovanili della Slovenia.

Attualmente impegnato nel settore giovanile del Voždovac, in Serbia, è un centrocampista offensivo mancino, dotato di una struttura fisica già importante nonostante la giovanissima età.

Un profilo che ha attirato l'attenzione di diversi osservatori internazionali e sul quale l'Inter ha deciso di muoversi con decisione.

Stefan Ćapin compirà infatti 16 anni il prossimo 13 gennaio 2027 e proprio durante la sessione invernale potrebbe arrivare in nerazzurro.

La trattativa non è ancora da considerarsi ufficialmente conclusa, ma l'Inter ha compiuto passi importanti, riuscendo a portarsi davanti alle altre pretendenti.

Un possibile investimento per il futuro, con il club nerazzurro intenzionato ad anticipare la concorrenza internazionale per assicurarsi un talento della generazione 2011.

#2248. Taylor, la Juventus torna alla carica: la Lazio chiede 60 milioni

Per il centrocampista olandese, già cercato in estate, l'ipotesi di offerta bianconera si aggira sui 40 milioni.

La Juventus sarebbe tornata sulle tracce di Taylor, centrocampista olandese della Lazio, e starebbe valutando un’offerta vicina ai 40 milioni di euro. Secondo quanto riportato da Calciomercato, Claudio Lotito, però, non avrebbe intenzione di cederlo per meno di 60 milioni. Il club bianconero vuole rafforzare il centrocampo già da gennaio.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Secondo quanto raccolto da Calciomercato.it, la Juventus aveva cercato Taylor con insistenza già durante la scorsa estate. Il giocatore, classe 2002, è tornato nel mirino dei bianconeri come possibile rinforzo per il centrocampo.

Taylor è tra gli uomini più importanti della formazione allenata da Gennaro Gattuso. La Lazio è prima in classifica dopo le prime dieci giornate, nelle quali ha ottenuto nove vittorie e un pareggio. L’interesse juventino riguarda dunque uno dei protagonisti della squadra biancoceleste.

La distanza economica tra le parti è di circa 20 milioni di euro: l’offerta della Juventus si aggirerebbe sui 40 milioni, mentre Lotito non vorrebbe scendere sotto i 60. L’interesse dei bianconeri per Taylor è concreto, ma l’intenzione di intervenire sul centrocampo da gennaio non coincide necessariamente con i tempi di un’eventuale operazione per il giocatore.

L’affare potrebbe infatti andare in porto in vista della prossima stagione. Molto dipenderà dalle competizioni che Lazio e Juventus disputeranno allora. La possibilità di un trasferimento resta quindi legata sia alla distanza tra la cifra ipotizzata per l’offerta e la richiesta di Lotito, sia agli impegni che attendono le due squadre nella stagione successiva.

"Mi piacerebbe ogni tanto venisse anche qualche altro compagno di squadra a dare qualche spiegazione, non sempre noi italiani. Ci metto la faccia come abbiamo sempre fatto". Queste le pesanti parole di Matteo Politano a Sky Sport dopo la debacle del Napoli sul campo del Porto.

Negli studi dell'emittente, Paolo Di Canio, ex calciatore, ha commentato così le parole dell'esterno: "Abbiamo vissuto tutti momenti di scazzo dopo una partita, ma non vai a puntare direttamente gli stranieri: non credo possa parlare di Hojlund, abbiamo tutti la percezione dell'impegno, non puoi imputargli nulla.

Quello che sta creando un po' di cose è un po' De Bruyne, che si crede superiore al contesto dove si trova perché se sta fuori è lesa maestà, dopo ci parli e lo rimetti in carreggiata. Arriva Politano quasi non pensando alla sconfitta ad indicare questa cosa. I giocatori devono trovare una soluzione come fa l'Inter, che è sana come società: quando non va qualcosa, si trovano perché hanno gli anticorpi, si guardano in faccia e ricominciano a correre nella stessa direzione".

#2246. Napoli Primavera, Nocerino: “Odio perdere, ma è importante vedere i ragazzi competere contro una squadra così forte”

Ecco le dichiarazioni rilasciate da Antonio Nocerino dopo il ko del Napoli Primavera in Youth League per 3-1 contro il Porto:

““La prestazione, soprattutto quella del secondo tempo, mi è piaciuta. Nel primo tempo, invece, sono un po’ rammaricato, perché non abbiamo giocato con lo stesso coraggio e la stessa sfacciataggine che poi si è vista nella ripresa. Abbiamo avuto più di qualche opportunità per fare gol, ma questo è calcio: perché abbiamo subito tre reti uguali, in ripartenza. Non sono felice, perché odio la sconfitta, ma è importante vedere i ragazzi competere con una squadra  davvero molto forte. Ci poteva stare un rigore per il Napoli? Ho quasi litigato con l’arbitro. Al di là dell’episodio, non mi è piaciuto come ha gestito la gara: Le gare di Champions vanno molto veloci, mentre quest’oggi è stato un match molto lento perché l’arbitro fischiava sempre. A prescindere, non mi attacco all’arbitro. Ricerca continua di soluzioni e di uomini? Facciamo delle buone prestazioni, perché chi gioca con noi ha un atteggiamento, voglia, senso di appartenenza, davvero grande. Quando indossi la maglia o la tuta del Napoli indossi un’armatura, perché noi dobbiamo rispettare chi lavora per noi. Noi dobbiamo meritare la fortuna di lavorare e giocare per la squadra della nostra città. Avrei voluto lo stesso atteggiamento a Monopoli? Sì, ma ci sono anche gli avversari: ma non voglio scuse. Abbiamo comunque perso due partite in dieci gare, vuol dire che qualcosa di buono è stato fatto. Potrei dire tante cose di quel match, ma non voglio dire nulla. Potevamo giocare meglio, può essere, ma la cosa che importa è che i ragazzi abbiamo una mentalità che rispecchi il Napoli: giocare con il Napoli è un piacere ed un onore, ma tutto questo va meritato. Io metto in campo chi ha il fuoco dentro, solo così possiamo competere con squadre così forti: con la fame. Solo così possiamo alzare il livello e farli crescere in maniera tranquilla: l’errore ci può stare, ma non  deve essere fatto con sufficienza. Questa è la mentalità che dobbiamo avere: le cose non sono dovute, ma devono essere guadagnate. Cosa serve tornare per tornare in Primavera 1? Noi dobbiamo guadagnarci le vittorie, non si vincono le gare a priori perché sei il Napoli, non si vincono solo con qualità e tecnica. Perché la Primavera 2 è un campionato che ti forma: è molto fisico, tanti duelli. La promozione non è scontata, ce la dobbiamo guadagnare e sudare. Dipende tutto dalla nostra  volontà nel lavorare e non dalla fortuna. Chiummariello e Lieto in panchina questa sera con la prima squadra? Sarò sempre soddisfatto quando i ragazzi della Primavera sono in prima squadra. Questo è il nostro lavoro: lavoro con i giovani, perché spero che i ragazzi abbiano l’opportunità e dimostrino di essere all’altezza di avere l’opportunità di stare con la prima squadra”.

#2245. Chelsea’s feisty friendly ends in penalty shoot-out confusion

Chelsea’s Far East tour ended in farce and confusion with players waiting around for a penalty shoot-out that never happened.

The chaos came at the end of a hard-earned, bad-tempered draw against Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim, with an own-goal in the 89th minute sparring the west London side’s blushes.

That goal also was supposed to set up penalties. But after minutes of waiting around – and Kevin Campello, Chelsea’s head of first-team operations, saying “it’s written in the contract” – the players walked off the pitch.

That confusion ended a feisty affair in which tensions threatened to boil over and that, at certain points, paid little attention to the “friendly” aspect of the clash with seven yellow cards shown. At one point the visitors’ new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee exchanged angry words with some of Johor’s coaching staff. The CFC TV commentary team suggested that the spot-kicks were abandoned because of the match’s heated atmosphere.

Austin MacPhee was ready to throw hands😂 pic.twitter.com/CFDgTOwmxE

Having played just 24 hours earlier in Jakarta – a 3-0 win over AC Milan – it was no surprise to see Xabi Alonso name a fresh XI, a mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters given much-needed game time.

And considering Johor are one game away from setting a new world record of 109 matches unbeaten in the top flight – a run that would surpass the current mark set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s – it was also no shock to see the Malaysian team offer a stern, pre-season test for the west Londoners.

After a good start Chelsea were second best in a first half in which Johor should have been at least two goals to the good. The Malaysian champions controlled the first 45 minutes and were 1-0 up after 14 minutes – a low cross from the left side-footed home by Arif Aiman.

The hosts gave the young, inexperienced Chelsea backline a torrid time, especially on the flanks and Óscar Arribas was guilty of not capitalising on a great chance to double Johor’s lead, his shot after cutting in from the right going wide.

While they looked vulnerable at the back, Chelsea also struggled to keep possession in attack. But they got an equaliser they scarcely deserved after Liam Delap was manhandled to the ground in the box by Kevin Medina. The striker, who may well leave Stamford Bridge before the transfer window slams shut, fired home the spot-kick allowing the visitors to go into the break on level terms.

For the most part, the second half followed a similar pattern to the first – Jofor having the better chances, while tensions on the pitch continued to run high.

It was, however, Chelsea who took the lead after the break, Delap once again scoring from the spot, this time after Jamie Gittens was brought down in the area.

Johor, though, kept on creating, thanks in part to a fairly porous visitors’ backline, and levelled through a deflected Arribas free kick, before going 3-2 up thanks thanks to a well-taken Bérgson strike.

Had it stayed that way Chelsea could have had few complaints. But as the clock approached 90 minutes, the visitors had one last attack. Mykhailo Mudryk, just on as a substitute, delivered a cross from the left that Antonio Glauder could only steer into his own net. That was supposed to set up the penalty shoot-out that did not take place and the chance for one of the sides to claim a hollow victory.

Considering a raft of changes and that fact this was far from the first XI, it is hard to know what to make of this. But among the positive things Alonso could take from the game was the impressive form of Nicolas Jackson and good centre-forward play of Delap. The negative was, however, a poor defensive display.

Chelsea return to Stamford Bridge on Saturday for their last pre-season friendly, against Real Sociedad, before the Premier League season starts away at local rivals Fulham on August 24.

Johor Darul Ta’zim: Syihan Hazmi; Arribas, Israfilov (Carlos Akapo 82), Medina, Antonio Glauder, Silva (La’Vere Corbin-Ong 89); Arif Aiman, Petrovic, Méndez (Nené 78), Marcos Guilherme (Bérgson); Zahedi (Stoichkov 62). Substitutes: Abad, Davies, Hidalgo, Nahuel Leiva, Lowry, Mohamadou Sumareh, Stuart Wilkin.Booked: Israfilov, Antonio Glauder, Silva.Goals: Arif Aiman (14), Arribas (65), Bérgson (86).Chelsea: Sharman-Lowe (Slolina 46); Subuloye, Adarabioyo, Anselmino (Watson 29); Geovany Quenda, Dario Essugo, Nicoll-Jazuli, Gittens (Mudryk 87); Estêvão, Delap, Jacskon (Satpaev 86). Substitutes: Curd, Diakite, Kavuma-McQueen, Sarr, Walsh.Booked: Estêvão, Delap, Jackson, Geovany Quenda, Watson.Goals: Delap (42 pen, 62 pen), Antonio Glauder (89 og).

There will NOT be a penalty shootout. No one is quite sure why.

Anyway, that was an entertaining draw, plenty of good things for Chelsea (the play of Delap and Jackson) as well as worrying signs (open and vulnerable at the back).

The commentators on CFC TV are now not so sure!

That was an entertaining pre-season friendly. There was a bit of niggle and that added to the action.

There will be penalties, apparently, if it stays the same score...

Will there be a late winner? There will be four minutes of added time.

Mudryk just on picks up the ball on the left and, with four Chelsea players in the box, crosses into the danger area. It’s a good ball and asks too many questions of the hosts as Glauder diverts the ball into his own net.

It’s what the host have, on the balance of play, deserved, but it’s a gift from Chelsea. Essugo loses the ball in the final third and Bergson, on as sub pick it put driving at the box before hitting a low shot from outside the area, the ball nestling in the left corner of the net.

Chelsea have been better this half than the first 45, they’ve been able to control the pace of the game well since the break.

The pace has slowed down since the break, Chelsea seeing more of the ball. They work it right before Watson loses possession on the edge of the area.

The referee clearly forgot about the hydration break and the two teams are having a belated one now. Delightful...

I reckon there’s another goal left in this match. It’s been entertaining fare and the hosts have given as good as they’ve got, if not more.

This has been a lively match, better than most run-of-the-mill pre-season friendlies. Chelsea seeing a fair bit of possession at the moment, can they fashion a chance?

Yes they can. But it’s a longish shot from Gittens that is easily saved by Hamzi in the JDT goal.

More niggle in this match that hasn’t really had many tough challenges. After a few handbags the referee takes control and the argy bargy peters out.

It’s the least the hosts deserve. They have a free-kick 25 yards out, Arribas takes it with his right it’s at the wall but in turning away from the ball Delap deflects it into the far-right corner giving Slonina no chance.

Fluky goal but the hosts have deserved their bit of luck.

Delap again with the goal, this time he goes low, but still to the keeper’s right.

Penalty for Chelsea. Gittens cuts back in the box onto his right and is clipped by the defender. Clear-cut penalty.

Half-chance for Delap on the edge of the area. He playes a one-two with Jackson before opening up his body and letting fly, the shot going well wide.

Another good chance for the hosts and it’s not shock to write that it’s come from the industry of Arribas on the right. He fires in a low cross that evades everyone in the box.

Estevao goes down in the box, it looks as though it could well be a penalty but the referee waves play on. The Brazilian is the shown a yellow card for possibly lashing out having not got the decision he wanted.

The hosts have asserted themselves well this half, in much the same way as they did in the first 45 minutes.

Another good chance for the hosts and again it’s all too easy as Zahedi is one-on-one with the keeper. The striker, however, dithers a bit too long and Slonina makes a fine save. JDT have had plenty of chances to add to their sole goal...

Chelsea have had a ragged start to this half.

Good work from JDT who keep the ball well in midfield before a throughball is played to the on-rushing Zahedi but Slonina comes out well.

They’re back under way in Johor, and there’s an early chance for Jackson who gets the ball in the box, but the ball gets stuck underneath him and he cannot get in a good attempt in on goal.

And that is the last action of an entertaining half. Chelsea started well before the hosts opened the scoring. JDT then took control of the half and should, if truth be told, have extended their lead. But Delap did well to earn the penalty that he subsequently scored and should have made it 2-1 with the last kick of the 45.

Worrying signs at the back, however, for Alonso. Will Chelsea go to four at the back after the break?

The answer to that question (see last post) was so very nearly yes...

Jackson plays in a peach of a through ball with the outside of his right foot, Delap is one-on-one with the keeper and looks for all the world as though he has to score. BUT he scuffs his shot wide.

There will be three minutes of added time. Can Chelsea head into the break with an unexpected lead?

Free-kick for Chelsea on the JDT byline. The ball is put deep into the box, it’s headed back by Tosin before the ball is blazed over the bar.

A minute later Tosin then let’s fly form 25 yards, the ball goes well over the bar.

The hosts should have been more than 1-0 to the good and now they’re drawing. Goals change matches...

Having won the penalty Delap fires the spotkick home, sending the keeper the the wrong way.

Penalty to Chelsea and it’s all thanks to good centre-forward play by Delap. He gets the ball in the box and Medina manhands him to the ground. The referee doesn’t hesitate before pointing to the spot.

Chelsea have struggled to create anything since the opening 15 minutes. They have no control at the front and none at the back currently.

As I type that JDT have another good chance to turn the 1-0 lead into a 2-0 lead. Arribas, whose been a menace all game, dances toward the Chelsea box before delaying the pass too long.

JDT are finding a lot of joy on the flanks, there are three at the back for Chelsea and on the outside are two youngsters. The hosts are working the space well.

Yet again Chelsea are made to look decidedly average. A simple ball over the top on the right opens up the visitors’ defence and Arribas is in on goal, he cuts in and lets fly with his left peg, the shot going wide.

That should have been 2-0 to the Malaysian powerhouses.

Worrying signs for Chelsea who have struggled to keep possession up top and looked vulnerable at the back.

Yet more good work from JDT who are being given space by Chelsea. Marcos Guilherme slaloms into the west Londoners’ box and Tosin again doesn’t look the most assured but the JDT player cuts the ball back and the visitors can clear the danger.

Another good attack from the hosts who get in a shot in on goal, it’s deflected and loops into the grateful arms of Sharman-Lowe in the Chelsea goal.

There’s a break in play with Anselmino down and suffering what looks like a hamstring injury. He is eventually replaced by Reggie Watson.

Meanwhile, the home fans are in fine voice and waving several HUGE flags.

Yep, everyone’s least favourite part of the World Cup in the U, S of A is back. To be fair it’s humid in Johor so taking on fluids during the first 45 minutes is no bad idea.

There’s a bit of argy-bargy not really what you should get in a ‘friendly’. There hasn’t been a bad chellenge in the match so far so not sure where that came from...

Yet more good work from the hosts, this time it’s down the right, Arribas getting the better of Anselmino before shooting at the near post - the attempt hitting the side netting.

After a lively start Chelsea have been second best.

Poor defending from the visitors there but the chance was well snapped up by JDT.

Lovely break from the hosts. They break down the left at pace, before the ball is threaded through to the back post and Arif Aiman sidefoots into the back of the net with aplomb.

So very nearly an opener for Chelsea. They break at pace thanks to Estevao who drives down the middle before playing in Jackson. The striker cuts in from the left and shoots, the attempt is saved well by Hamzi and Estevao’s follow up is wide. Is a goal coming?

Free-kick for Chelsea some 35 yards out. Too far fro a shot on goal? Of course it is. The ball is floated into the box and the visitors earn a corner.

What can they create from this set piece? ‘Not much’ is the initial answer as the ball is cleared by JDT but Chelsea win possession back and the ball is fed to Estevao on the left, the Brazilian goes for go with his trusty left peg but the bal goes high and wide.

JDT attack down the left, it’s a lovely ball in that forces a fine header to clear the danger from Adarabioyo.

No sooner had I sent that last post than Chelsea break through the middle. The ball is fed through to Delap who gets a left-footed shot in on goal forcing a good save from the JDT keeper Hamzi.

Quiet, low-key start to the match. No real shock there, it is a pre-season friendly.

JDT give the ball away in their half and Chelsea have a half-decent platform to launch an attack from. They cannot fashion a chance and also lose possession.

They’re under way in southern Malaysia, Chelsea are in their vibrant blue and the hosts are wearing a fetching pink number. There was a late change for the visitors, Mamadou Sarr has been replaced by Olutayo Subuloye.

CHELSEA XI TO FACE JOHOR: Sharman-Lowe; Sarr, Tosin, Anselmino; Quenda, Nicoll-Jazuli, Essugo (c), Gittens; Estevao; Jackson, Delap; subs: Slonina, Curd, Subuloye, Diakite, Watson, Mudryk, Walsh, Kavuma-McQueen, Satpayev

...Luis Garcia. The Spaniard has history with Chelsea, remember the ‘ghost goal’?

Arriving for duty! 🫡 pic.twitter.com/M2XEkLC18n

Your Chelsea side today! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0OvvGVmgpc

A mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters you may not have heard of.

Johor Darul Ta’Zim – more commonly known as JDT – are the Man Utd of Malaysia (at least that’s according to a Malaysian friend of mine). In 2013, they were going nowhere and were the dictionary definition of a stagnant club, low on confidence and trophies. That was until the Crown Prince bought the club and, over the next 13 years, transformed it into the powerhouse it is today.

As if to underline JDT’s dominance over Malaysian football they are one game away from the world record unbeaten run in a top flight. The new season of the Malaysian Super League gets under way later this month and should they avoid defeat in their opening match they will extend their unbeaten run - which began in April 2021 - to 109 games and surpass the world record set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s.

Chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

“The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

“We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our plan and we’ve stuck to that.

“We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”

Stay here for all the team news and action with kick-off set for 1pm.

#2244. SPFL reveals Rangers vs Hibs final date, time, ticket split and prices

Rangers and Hibernian have been handed a 50/50 split of Hampden for next month’s Premier Sports Cup final.

The sides will meet at the national stadium on Sunday, December 13, with the showpiece scheduled for a 3pm kick-off and broadcast live on Premier Sports.

Confirmed match arrangements and ticket information for next month's 2026/27 Premier Sports Cup final 🏆 https://t.co/Iaq1uil4L4

The SPFL has confirmed the ticketing arrangements following discussions with both clubs and the relevant authorities.

Hibernian supporters will be housed across the South, East and North Stands, while Rangers fans will be located across the South, West and North Stands.

Ticket prices will be the same for both sets of supporters.

The majority of adult tickets will cost £42, with adult seats in the North and South Stands priced at £49.

Concessionary tickets will also be available across the stadium, priced at £27 or £30 depending on the section.

Rangers secured their place in the final by defeating Aberdeen last Saturday, with Ryan Naderi scoring a late winner in the semi-final.

Hibernian booked their Hampden return a day later with a 2-1 victory over Edinburgh rivals Hearts.

All tickets will be issued digitally through the Barclays Hampden app, with both clubs set to announce their respective sales information through their own channels.

It will be only the second time Rangers and Hibs have met in the final of the competition.

Their previous meeting came in the 1993/94 final at Celtic Park, when Rangers won 2-1.

#2243. Alta tensione Napoli: lite in campo tra Lucca e De Bruyne, volano parole pesanti! La ricostruzione

Alta tensione Napoli: lite in campo tra Lucca e De Bruyne, volano parole pesanti! La ricostruzione

Installa la nostra App gratuita e accedi più velocemente alle notizie

Volano stracci in casa Napoli dopo il ko per 4-1 contro il Porto in Champions League. Succede tutto nella ripresa, subito dopo il momentaneo 3-1 dei lusitani. Secondo quanto riportato in telecronaca su Prime Video c'è stato un acceso battibecco tra Kevin De Bruyne e Lorenzo Lucca.

Lo scontro è avvenuto intorno all'82', sul risultato appunto di 3-1 per il Porto dopo un un'azione offensiva del Napoli. “È stata una scena non bella da vedere. Nervosismo in casa Napoli”, hanno commentato Sandro Piccinini e Massimo Ambrosini.

Il centrocampista belga e l’attaccante italiano si sono fronteggiati a muso duro nel finale di partita con alcuni gesti molto plateali a ridosso dell’area del Porto. Dopo una strigliata di De Bruyne, Lucca si è rivolto al compagno di squadra così, come ricostruito dai colleghi di Amazon Prime Video: "Perché parli? Perché parli? Va*******o". Un episodio di grande tensione in un momento davvero delicato per la squadra di Allegri, sia in Serie A che in Champions.

#2242. A San Siro arriva il Como, il retroscena su Nico Paz: “Ai dirigenti Inter ha detto queste parole"

A San Siro arriva il Como, il retroscena su Nico Paz: “Ai dirigenti Inter ha detto queste parole"

Installa la nostra App gratuita e accedi più velocemente alle notizie

Mentre navighi nell'app, scorri il dito da sinistra a destra dello schermo per tornare alle pagine precedenti

6 gol e 8 assist in 13 partite totali tra Serie A e Champions League: numeri da urlo per Nico Paz in questa prima parte di stagione col Como. In estate il suo nome era stato accostato all’Inter soprattutto a inizio mercato. Ma cosa c’era di vero?

A mercato chiuso, Fabrizio Romano ha svelato quanto segue proprio su Nico Paz e l’Inter. “Nico Paz la scorsa estate doveva rientrare al Real Madrid, ma il Como ci ha sempre creduto nel riuscire a contare sulla sua volontà. Posso rivelarvi che Nico ha detto in una chiamata diretta con Jose Mourinho: "Grazie mister per la stima ma voglio restare al Como, penso sia fondamentale per giocarle tutte e crescere". Mourinho e il Real, che ci contavano, si sono ritrovati un ragazzo che ha preferito restare a Como.

Quando il Real attiva la recompra, il Como rimane in silenzio nonostante la tempesta mediatica di circa 24 ore. Si parlava tanto dell'Inter: l'Inter avrebbe voluto provarci ma lui è stato molto onesto dicendo qeste parole: "Io voglio stare al Como". Quel famoso discorso Inter è morto ancora prima di cominciare perché tutto ruotava attorno al Como che ha mantenuto la sua tranquillità forte dell'ok del giocatore”. Ora se lo gode il Como, che arriverà a San Siro proprio contro i nerazzurri per la prossima giornata di Serie A.

#2241. Napoli-Lazio, tifosi ospiti verso lo stop: atteso il decreto della Prefettura

Il divieto dovrebbe riguardare anche gli altri settori del Maradona per chi risiede nella Regione Lazio.

Il settore ospiti del Maradona dovrebbe restare chiuso per Napoli-Lazio, in programma domenica 8 novembre alle 12:30. Secondo quanto riportato da Radio Laziale, la trasferta sarà vietata ai sostenitori biancocelesti. La decisione non è ancora ufficiale: si attende il decreto della Prefettura di Napoli, previsto tra oggi e domani.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Il provvedimento dovrebbe impedire ai residenti nella Regione Lazio di acquistare biglietti per la partita. La restrizione non riguarderebbe soltanto il settore ospiti, ma anche gli altri settori dello stadio Diego Armando Maradona. Per i tifosi la notizia arriva dopo settimane segnate da una forte partecipazione alle trasferte della squadra.

Nei giorni scorsi l’Osservatorio Nazionale sulle Manifestazioni Sportive (ONMS) aveva rinviato la valutazione della gara al Comitato di Analisi per la Sicurezza delle Manifestazioni Sportive (CASMS). L’Osservatorio aveva inoltre invitato a non avviare la vendita dei biglietti destinati ai sostenitori ospiti.

Il quadro, secondo le indiscrezioni, sarebbe ora orientato verso la conferma del divieto e la chiusura del settore riservato ai tifosi della Lazio. Resta da attendere il decreto della Prefettura di Napoli: sarà il provvedimento ufficiale a formalizzare le restrizioni e a definirne le modalità di applicazione.

Se l’orientamento sarà confermato, la Lazio affronterà la trasferta senza i propri sostenitori provenienti dal territorio laziale. La limitazione all’acquisto dei biglietti, così come prospettata, si estenderebbe anche ai posti fuori dal settore ospiti.

Il possibile stop arriverebbe dopo una serie di partite lontano dall’Olimpico seguite da migliaia di sostenitori biancocelesti. A Reggio Emilia, in particolare, circa 10mila tifosi della Lazio hanno accompagnato la squadra, con una presenza significativa sugli spalti.

La partecipazione delle ultime settimane aveva alimentato le aspettative anche per la sfida al Maradona. Per i sostenitori, la partita con il Napoli rappresentava un appuntamento sentito sia per il valore della gara sia per la volontà di continuare a seguire la formazione biancoceleste in trasferta.

Il divieto interromperebbe questa sequenza di trasferte molto partecipate. Dopo l’esodo di Reggio Emilia, i tifosi residenti nel Lazio rischiano dunque di non poter assistere alla partita di Napoli, neppure acquistando un posto in un settore diverso da quello ospiti.

#2240. Rangers youth prospect reveals personal ‘privilege’ of working with boyhood hero

Rangers youngster Rydnn McGuire has opened up on the “privilege” of working alongside his former goalkeeping hero Allan McGregor at Ibrox.

McGregor returned to Rangers as a coach and is now helping develop the next generation of goalkeepers, including McGuire, who has spent time around the first-team set-up this season.

🗣️ "It's a chance for everyone to go and showcase their skills to a lot of people." Rydnn McGuire spoke to @RangersTV ahead of tomorrow evening's #UYL second leg clash against Dynamo Kyiv at Forthbank Stadium. 🎟️ https://t.co/dzAtggjPPN https://t.co/kA5EgInsvc

— Rangers Academy (@RFC_Youth) November 3, 2026

Speaking to Rangers club media ahead of Wednesday’s UEFA Youth League second leg against Dynamo Kyiv, McGuire revealed he grew up watching the former Scotland international.

He said: “Very good. It’s a privilege to come and work with him every day.

“He was probably my generation of Rangers goalie growing up, so I watched him from a young age, and he’s been really good to work with.”

McGuire has combined his involvement around the senior squad with appearances in the KDM Evolution Trophy and Youth League this season.

The young goalkeeper believes that mixture has been important for his development rather than simply training without getting competitive minutes.

He said: “I think it’s critical in what I need just now.

“To come down and play these games, and they’re high-level games, they are challenging games that I’m coming down and playing, so it’s getting experience from everything.”

McGuire was part of the Rangers youth side whose success last season earned them the chance to compete in Europe and was determined not to miss out after making the step up to the first-team environment.

He said: “It was the first thing I said to Greegsie when I went round. I don’t want all the hard work I did last year to go to waste and not getting to get to play in it, so I made sure my stance was that I wanted to play in these games.

“They’ve been really good, and they have let me play in these games, so a massive thanks to them for letting me do that.”

Russell Martin ‘spoken highly of’ at Manchester United before Rangers stint

Pedro Caixinha back in Europe after joining 13th club of managerial career

Unseen moment Rangers star warned 'job's not done' by team-mate after semi-final win

Attention now turns to Wednesday’s return against Dynamo Kyiv, with Rangers still in the tie due to the 3-2 scoreline, following two second-half goals in the first leg.

McGuire admits the Light Blues will have to produce an almost flawless performance if they are to progress.

He said: “The information we’re getting from Stevie and the staff, we believe we can go and pull it off. We probably need to be as close to perfect as we can on Wednesday.

“We can’t afford to slip up in any way; we need to be perfect in all senses to get the result we want.”

McGuire was impressed by the quality of the Ukrainian side in his first experience of European club football, highlighting their attacking threat in particular.

He added: “I think individual qualities in that team were outstanding. I think the striker and the winger were really good.

“I knew they’d be decent players, I knew they’d be a decent team, and they were, but a few top, top players that can hurt us on Wednesday.”

#2239. Di Canio: “Inter ambiente sano, negli anni hanno costruito gli anticorpi! Quando non va qualcosa..."

Di Canio: “Inter ambiente sano, negli anni hanno costruito gli anticorpi! Quando non va qualcosa..."

Installa la nostra App gratuita e accedi più velocemente alle notizie

Mentre navighi nell'app, scorri il dito da sinistra a destra dello schermo per tornare alle pagine precedenti

In studio a Sky Sport, l'ex attaccante Paolo Di Canio ha parlato così dei momenti di Inter e Napoli dopo le gare di Champions League.

“La situazione dell’Inter è diversa da quella del Napoli. Il gruppo del Napoli è finito, esausto, anche psico-fisicamente. L’Inter è una cosa totalmente diversa: un ambiente che ha costruito anticorpi.

Qualcosa non va? Ci si trova e si dice tutto, si corre tutti nella stessa direzione perché l’ambiente è sano. Al Napoli non mi sembra ci sia”.

#2238. RILEGGI LIVE – Porto-Napoli 4-1 (11′ Bednarek, 43′ McTominay, 71′ Gabri Veiga, 80′ Kiwior, 89′ Samu su rig.), gli azzurri cadono in Portogallo

89′ Gol Porto: Samu spiazza Meret dal dischetto

88′ Calcio di rigore Porto: Rafa Marin espulso per fallo da ultimo uomo su Samu, solo davanti alla porta.

80′ Gol Porto: ancora su corner Kiwior chiude i giochi

78′ Fuori Gabri Veiga e Pepe, dentro Fofana e Hwang

75′ Contropiede Porto: Samu non serve compagno solo e va al tiro, blocca Meret

71′ Gol Porto: lusitani nuovamente avanti con Gabri Veiga

66′ Dentro Gimenez e Zaidu, fuori Sainz e Fernandes.

62′ Missile di Samu che colpisce la traversa

59′ Tiro di McTominay, blocca il portiere

56′ Corner e ancora Bednarek sfiora la doppietta

54′ Rrahmani salva su Alberto Costa, Porto all’attacco.

50′ Errore di Politano, Meret salva su Rosario in due tempi

43′ GOOOL NAPOLI: Diogo Costa salva prima su Politano e poi su Hojlund, alla terza occasione McTominay insacca

42′ Cross basso di Vergara, Hojlund non ci arriva per poco

38′ Gol annullato a De Bruyne per fuorigioco

37′ Gabri Veiga sfiora il palo, palla sull’esterno della rete

36′ Ammonito anche McTominay per fallo su Froholdt

35′ Ammonito Rrahmani che ferma una ripartenza

29′ Grande azione di Hojlund che parte dalla sua metà campo, ne dribbla due e il suo tiro deviato termina di poco a lato

25′ Cross pericoloso di Pepe, Marin chiude e salva in extremis

20′ Anguissa ammonito per fallo su Gabri Veiga

13′ Hojlund cade a terra in area, per l’arbitro non c’è nulla.

11′ Gol Porto: su calcio d’angolo Bednarek insacca di testa anticipando tutti

7′ Tiro a giro di Borja Sainz, palla di poco alta

6′ Cross pericoloso Porto, Beukema spazza in corner

5′ Ci prova Hojlund dal limite, mura la difesa

3′ Pepe insacca in rete, l’arbitro ferma tutto per fuorigioco

2′ Cross di Politano, tiro di McTominay che termina alto

1′ Ammonito Vergara per un fallo piuttosto duro

PORTO (4-3-3): Diogo Costa; Martim Fernandes, Bednarek, Kiwior, Alberto Costa; Gabriel Veiga, Rosario, Froholdt; Sainz, André Silva, Pepê. A disposizione: Claudio Ramos, Joao Costa, Samu, Sanusi, IB Hwang, Nehuen Perez, Varela, Gimenez, Souza, Fofana, Francisco Moura, Pietruszewski. All. Farioli.

NAPOLI (3-5-1-1): Meret; Beukema, Rafa Marín, Rrahmani; Politano, Anguissa, Gilmour, McTominay, Vergara; De Bruyne; Hojlund. A disposizione: Contini, Milinkovic-Savic, Lucca, Giovane, Chiummariello, Lieto, Lang. All. Allegri.

Benvenuti alla diretta testuale del match valido per la quarta giornata di Champions League tra Porto e Napoli. La squadra di Allegri è in grande emergenza ma proverà a fare risultato in Portogallo.
